about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: No fresh supply news overnight; prices are steadying after Wednesday's dollar-driven slide. With Dec in its delivery period, certificated flow and the high-grade share of certs set the tone for old-crop, and those are not a comfort for longs until Mar takes over.
events: Dec cotton slid with outside markets Wednesday, holding near 75 (Barchart)
Texas yield trimmed again in USDA's November crop report (RFD-TV)

sugar.fundamental: Brazil still sets the tone: the real fell another ~1.9% this morning, which encourages more Brazilian raw-sugar export pricing and keeps Mar near 17.9. Tereos cutting its outlook on a poor French beet crop is a small European offset, not enough to change the Brazil-led bias.
events: Real weakens again; Mar raws ~17.92 (Yahoo Finance)
Tereos cuts profit outlook after a poor French beet harvest (Investing.com)
USDA outlook sees lower world sugar output (ADMIS)

coffee.fundamental: Bigger expected Brazil supplies and a weaker real keep pressure on flat price (Dec ~280). Deliverability still leans tight, though: falling ICE certified arabica stocks remain the counterweight and the key thing to watch into the Dec/Mar spread.
events: Arabica eased on larger Brazil and global supply expectations (Barchart)
Brazilian real down ~1.9% Thursday, encouraging producer selling (Yahoo Finance)
ICE certified arabica stocks keep declining (ICE)

cocoa.fundamental: A modest bounce (Dec ~4,924, +1.6%) after Wednesday's drop, but nothing new on supply: rising ICE stocks and better West African crop prospects still dominate, while rain-slowed Ivorian port deliveries are a passing factor.
events: Cocoa bounced ~1.6% early Thursday after Wednesday's slide (Yahoo Finance)
Improved supply prospects and rising ICE stocks weigh (Barchart)
Ghana plans to phase out raw bean exports by 2030 (Reuters)
